spotlights.label: Crash becomes an empty 200
spotlights.why: Before, a route calling c.HTML with no templates loaded panicked: under gin.Default() Recovery answered 500 and logged a stack trace; under gin.New() the connection dropped. Now the client gets the handler's own status (200) with an empty text/html body, and the error lives only in c.Errors. With gin.New() and no Logger, nothing is logged at all.

spotlights.label: 204 and 304 now pass without complaint
spotlights.why: With no renderer, a 204 or 304 never reaches HTML.Render, so no error is recorded, the context is not aborted and later handlers run. A missing renderer goes unnoticed on those routes.

spotlights.label: Custom renderers with nil templates change too
spotlights.why: The nil check lives in render.HTML, so any HTMLRender whose Instance returns HTML{Template: nil} now gets the error instead of a panic, not only the unset-renderer case.

spotlights.label: The new error is not exported
spotlights.why: errHTMLRendererNotConfigured is package-private, so callers inspecting c.Errors can only match it by its text, not with errors.Is.

steps.title: Make an HTML render with no template return an error
steps.why: Adds the errHTMLRendererNotConfigured sentinel and checks r.Template for nil in HTML.Render, after the Content-Type is written and before the template is executed.
steps.consequence: render.HTML{} renders to an error with a text/html header and no body, instead of dereferencing a nil template. Nothing calls it that way yet.

notes: Runs first: header set even on error

steps.title: Send c.HTML through Render when no renderer is set
steps.why: Context.HTML used to call c.engine.HTMLRender.Instance unconditionally, which panics on a nil interface. Now, when HTMLRender is nil, it hands an empty render.HTML{} to c.Render.
steps.consequence: For a status with a body, c.Render records the error with c.Error and aborts; for 1xx, 204 and 304 it writes only the header, as before. No status is changed to 500.

notes: Old code panicked on this nil
Template nil: Render returns the error

steps.title: Prove GET, 204, 304 and HEAD without a renderer
steps.why: A table test drives c.HTML through a real router with no templates loaded and a second handler, and a unit test renders HTML{} directly.
steps.consequence: Each case asserts no panic, the handler's status, text/html, an empty body, and whether the error, abort and next handler happen.

notes: HEAD takes the GET error path
